newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says reviewing its insurance ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says reviewing its insurance ratings.

text.p: European rating agency IBCA said on Tuesday it was reviewing its insurance ratings and will re-release them to reflect its rating perspective.

The move followed the withdrawal of ratings assigned by Quest Insurance Research, in which IBCA took a 75 percent stake in April. The withdrawal affected more than 100 rating opinions on British property and casualty insurance companies, IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said its insurance methodology includes a redefined product line. It has replaced its Formal Security Rating (FSR) with a Claims Settling Ability (CSA) rating.

IBCA said it conducts investigations into the financial security of the insurer. The informal assessment, now known as the IQ Report, has been reformatted but still provides readers with an opinion of a company derived from public information, the rating agency said.
Whereas Quest offered opinion on property/casualty and healthcare insurers using the same analytical model, IBCA said it was developing separate models for these sectors as well as a Life model.
"Reinsurers will be assessed using the model most appropriate to the type of business written by the company," IBCA said.
Although development work is continuing, IBCA has confirmed several Claims Settling Ability ratings following its review.
Lombard General Insurance UK A plus
IBCA Quest is the vehicle through which IBCA will develop its international insurance rating services.
IBCA said it was originally established as a bank credit rating agency but now also offers rating services in corporates, sovereigns, supra- and sub-nationals, securitisation and insurance.
